answer: Tie voting weight to a non-transferable work ledger no farm can mint in one burst. A key may grade or vote only after posting an append-only log of twelve peer-signed jobs spanning four closed epochs, each countersigned by a distinct established peer and folded into a Merkle root. A seat is granted when that root is recorded as an anchor in the live state and job times do not form a tight spiral of same-hour signups. A mesa of keys spun up today has no such history, and a copied log fails because each leaf signature names one public key. Weight follows aged, diversified work, not headcount.
